Shri Pramod Singh Thakur - Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Tapan Bathre - Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State.

Order 
This is the first application filed on behalf of the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS) r/w Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.226/2024 registered at Police Station Chicholi, District Betul, for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(N) of the Indian Penal Code and Section 5(L)/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The applicant is in jail since 29.08.2024.
2.

Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that as per the case of prosecution, the prosecutrix is below 18 years, although, as per her statement, she with her own had gone with the applicant and they started living together as husband and wife and virtually they entered into the marriage.
They have been living together for almost one year and thereafter on the basis of missing report, they got arrested by the police.

The counsel for the petitioner has further submitted that from the statement of the prosecutrix, it is clear that the applicant has not committed any forceful act with her and has not harassed her in any NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:6008 2 MCRC-5277-2025 manner, but under innocency and presumption that the prosecutrix was major,
the applicant has developed physical relation and according to him, the age of the prosecutrix has not been properly shown.

He has submitted that the prosecutrix has already been recorded and nothing more is required to be inquired about from the applicant and under such circumstances, the Golu @ Mahendra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143820818/
1 applicant may be released from jail.
3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, the counsel for the State has opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that looking to the nature of crime and the age of the prosecutrix, the bail application deserves to be dismissed.

4. Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perusal of case diary and the fact that the applicant is in jail since 29.08.2024 and the prosecutrix has already been examined,
I am inclined to allow this bail application.
Therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

5. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.
6. On being released on bail, the applicant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 480(3) of BNSS.

(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE ac/-
